transcript: 90 % of traders are unprofitable because 90 % don't know this one rule about IFVGs, and it's the one reason I'm able to catch insane trades like this almost every single day. What you need to understand is that inverse fair value gaps are simply confirmation for the analysis you should have already made. IFVGs without proper context are what I refer to as coincidental inversions, and if you consistently use them, you'll definitely become one of the 90 % of traders whose trades consistently look like this. So how do you know which inverse fair value gaps are actually going to play out? Well, it's simple. Going to the day, the first thing you want to do is mark out two key levels, the nearest swing high above price, and the nearest swing low below price. Now that you have those marked out, you're going to want to wait for price to hit one of those key levels, and as you can see in this case, we perfectly hit this swing low. Next, you want to zoom in and find some sort of bearish trend line. In this case, I see this super obvious internal trend line. Now that we have all these marked out, you can go ahead and finally look for your inverse fair value gap. But wait, there's one more step to confirm that this is true confirmation. To confirm that this is a valid inverse fair value gap, and price is actually going to move up, we want to see the inversion candle close above the bearish trend line that we have marked out. And as you can see in this case, it perfectly does. This gives us all the confirmation we need to enter a long position, making sure our stop loss is protected by the trend line and targeting the key swing high that we had marked out earlier. Now all we do is watch the trade play out and if you want a full guide explaining exactly how I find trades like this every day, just comment model and I'll send it to you for free.
